grammar.provenance: the FULL produced vocabulary (100 types, named + anonymous) is enumerated in validation/m60/lua/grammar-inventory.json with a per-type count, because a COUNT cannot be argued with: a reader cannot check whether the node type that would express a construct is in the set when the set is not written down. That file also records, per ruled type, the node types that WOULD mean the construct exists and whether the grammar produced any of them. The 43 named types above are the subset of the 100 that the grammar declares as named nodes; the remaining 57 are anonymous tokens (`+`, `..`, `end`, `{`, `::`, …), which are counted in the artifact and omitted here because a token cannot be the grammatical evidence for a declaration.

_authority: script/m60/lua-ontology-census.ts (three instruments: production counts through `parseFile`, instrument A grammar inventory, instrument B parse-tree construct counts) and script/m60/lua-grammar-inventory.ts (instrument A as a standalone artifact). There is NO independent lua truth oracle in script/m14/oracles/, so every claim here rests on the analyzer plus a second instrument that does not share its rule table — never on the analyzer agreeing with itself.

corpus.sampling: every `git ls-files '*.lua'` path in every corpus repo, sorted, no cap. Deterministic and identical on every machine; not a random sample.
corpus.note: The census sample and the ontology gate's admitted set are both 3,250, because both enumerate the same predicate — tracked `*.lua` under a git repo. The gate additionally applies `detectLanguageFromPath`, which admits all 3,250.

design_decision.description: Owner rulings. Each is a deliberate refusal to publish, not a silence.

decisions.question: Which of the 10 relationship types does lua emit, and why is the rest inapplicable?
decisions.resolution: RULED ONCE, AFTER BEING WRONG FOUR TIMES. NINE are emitted — calls, uses, contains, imports, references, exports, extends, overrides, instantiates — and ONE is ruled: `implements`. The revisions are the substance of this decision, because each one was a ruling that measurement refused. `uses` was ruled inapplicable (a name read is not a dependency); probe B4 then counted 295,019 bare-name reads across 3,116 of 3,250 files and it is now 133,192 edges in 2,666. `references` was ruled inapplicable (a member read is a call); probe B3 counted 198,720 qualified reads across 2,643 files and it is now 44,757 edges in 2,340. `exports` was ruled inapplicable, which was true of the RELATIONSHIP and false of the FACT — the analyzer was already publishing 5,167 export names into `result.exports`, so the surface existed, was named, and no edge said so; it is now 5,167 edges in 2,137 files. `overrides` was ruled inapplicable, and that ruling was WRONG in the way this workstream exists to catch: the lua grammar produces 100 node types and none of them is `override_specifier` or `redefinition`, so a grammar inventory is silent here BY CONSTRUCTION, exactly as it is silent for json's `exports`. Instrument B found 65 redefinitions across 37 files, and the type is now 66 edges in 38 files. The lesson generalises to the family: a grammar cannot see a CONVENTION, and Lua's inheritance and module surface are both conventions over ordinary constructs. What remains excluded is `implements` and ONLY `implements` — see BD-implements, which is the one ruling here that instrument A settles on its own.

decisions.question: Does lua express a conformance relation distinct from a supertype link, and is `implements` therefore inapplicable?
decisions.resolution: RULED, and `implements` is the type it rules. Instrument A: the pinned grammar produced 100 distinct node types across 1,875 corpus files (validation/m60/lua/grammar-inventory.json), and NONE of the six node types that would express it is among them — `implements_clause`, `extends_clause`, `superclass`, `interface_implementation`, `interface_declaration`, `trait_declaration`. Lua has no `class` keyword, no `interface` keyword and no declaration form for a type at all, so the construct has no grammatical shape for an `implements` edge to be derived from; that is a fact about the language, not a failure to find something. Instrument B, for the relation that IS expressible: probe B6 counted 1,295 supertype links across 453 files, and every one of them is the SAME relation `extends` already publishes — probe B8 split them into four buckets over 501 links: 79 `crossTable` (derived and base are both declared tables), 45 `derivedIsSelf` (written as `setmetatable(self, …)` inside a constructor), 3 `selfLink` (derived equals base), and 374 `unresolvedBase` (the base argument is an EXPRESSION, e.g. `setmetatable(opts or {}, defaults)` at kong/kong/api/arguments.lua, so no name is written for it). Only the 79 carry a named base on both sides, and of those the analyzer emits 1 override because an override additionally requires a MEMBER both tables declare. A language with exactly one type relation cannot have a second one: conformance in Lua is DUCK TYPING, structural and undeclared, so there is no written clause naming a conformed-to type for an `implements` edge to carry. WHAT WOULD OVERTURN THIS RULING, stated so it can be falsified: a non-zero count of any of the six node types above in the instrument-A artifact, which is what a Lua dialect with a `class`/`interface` declaration would introduce; or a probe finding a constructor-like call immediately followed by a conformance test (`if type(x) ~= "table" then error(...) end`) at a rate worth an edge. Probe B8's `crossTable` bucket is the closest thing to a counter-example this corpus contains and it measures 1.

decisions.question: Which of the two things 'override' can mean in Lua does the emitted edge claim, and does the target use the member's own name?
decisions.resolution: RULED, and the ruling is a refusal to fuse. Lua writes TWO distinct constructs that a single label would conflate: a same-name redefinition in one chunk, where the later `function` replaces the earlier one (probe B1: 65 occurrences across 37 files), and a member of a derived table that shadows an inherited member through `__index` (probe B8: 1 cross-table site). They are emitted under two `meta.relationshipType` values — `lua_redefinition` at confidence 1.0 and `lua_inherited_member` at 0.95, the family's own numbers for the same two cases (real-bash-analyzer.ts:343, real-objective-c-analyzer.ts:1020) — so a consumer can count either without the other. The TARGET is the member's OWN NAME (`Derived` -> `run`) and never the qualified path (`Derived` -> `Derived.run`), because this lane's member-identity contract (LUA-15, pinned by validation/m14/fixtures/lua/member-identity.expectation.json) holds that the identity is container plus own name; the path is metadata (`meta.qualifiedName`, `meta.memberPath`). Measured consequence: the first version, which put the label in the target, produced labelShape {bare 54, dotted 8, colon 4} across the corpus and made the edge unjoinable to the `contains` edge for the same member. NOT CLAIMED: a `setmetatable(self, …)` inside a constructor — probe B8's `derivedIsSelf` bucket, 45 sites across 42 files. Nor the `unresolvedBase` bucket, 374 sites across 218 files, where the base is an expression and therefore has no written name. The derived table is only reachable by evaluating the constructor, and nothing in the parse tree says which table it returns, so closing those edges would require interprocedural evaluation rather than reading. That is stated as a limit, not as a ruling, because it is not a claim about the language.

decisions.question: Can a relationship rule test which node it is looking at by object identity?
decisions.resolution: RULED: no, and the ruling is enforced in code by `isSameNode` (real-lua-analyzer.ts), which compares `type` + `startIndex` + `endIndex`. `web-tree-sitter` returns a FRESH wrapper object on every access, so `parent.namedChild(0) === node` is false even when both name the same span. Measured cost of getting this wrong: the `uses`/`references` exclusions never fired, publishing 3 edges on the 15-line fixture lua/name-reads.lua that each state one qualified access twice under two labels, and dropping that fixture from 26 edges to 19 and lua/export-shapes from 25 to 16. This is the family's idiom rather than a local invention — real-c-analyzer.ts:2336, :2525 and :6012 all compare spans for this reason. REGRESSION-PINNED by script/m60/mutate-lua-node-identity.ts, which re-derives the identity comparison from the fixed source, requires the suite to go red under it, and restores the file: 4 forbid rows fail, and the restore is re-verified green.

decisions.question: Which relationship types does the lua differential audit, and what does it therefore prove?
decisions.resolution: RULED: the differential can only audit what its oracle implements, and there is NO lua entry in script/m14/oracles/, so every lua type in this wave is a DERIVATION finding — emitted by the analyzer and compared against nothing. That count is 9 of 9 emitted types and it is the largest single limitation on this lane's claims. It is also the reason the ontology gate exists: two implementations that both say nothing agree perfectly, which is how `uses`, `references`, `exports` and `overrides` were all absent from both paths and the differential stayed green throughout. The instrument that caught them was measuring the LANGUAGE (probes B1, B3, B4, B6, B8) rather than diffing the CODE. Writing a lua truth oracle is shared work in script/m14/ (§8) and is not this lane's to add; the precise requirement is recorded in the handover report.

decisions.question: `npx tsx script/m14/incoming-gate.ts lua lua 60` reads 1,305 ambiguous + 2,222 unresolved of 5,415 edges. Which of the 2,222 are external, which are in-corpus targets that must resolve, and which are irreducible?
decisions.resolution:
RULED WITH COUNTS: the unresolved column is HALF SAMPLE REACH, and the evidence is the same rule applied to a complete key space. `npx tsx validation/m14/fixtures/lua/incoming-split.mts --nf 60 --all` (its rule is IMPORTED from script/m14/incoming-rule.ts, and it re-measures the gate's five columns exactly: `COMPARE ... AGREE`) parses all 3,250 admitted files and classifies the sample's 2,222 unresolved edges against the COMPLETE project key space:

  declared in the SAME project   1,112 (50.0%)  — of which 297 have exactly one declaration (would read `resolved`) and 815 collide (would read `ambiguous`). A sample of 60 of 3,250 files truncates each project's symbol table, so a name whose collision lives in an unsampled file reads unique or unresolved here. THIS IS THE SAMPLE, NOT THE ANALYZER.
  declared in the CORPUS, another project   417 (18.8%)  — production resolves `WHERE s.project_id = ?`, so a name another repository declares is not a resolvable edge for this one, and it is not a defect either.
  declared NOWHERE   693 (31.2%)  — the irreducible residue, and it is classified rather than waved at: 232 bare `calls` (`uint8`, `uint32`, `string` — free names Lua binds through `_ENV`, host globals in the Wireshark/Kong surfaces), 222 bare `references` that carry a `receiver` (field reads: `prefs`, `ports`), 125 dotted `imports` (module paths: `ngx.semaphore`, `kong.db.schema.typedefs` — 105 of the 125 have a LEAF the project declares, so they name a module rather than a symbol), 40 bare `uses`, 38 `Upper` constant references (`DEC`, `HEX` — fields), 10 `hyphen` references (HTTP header names), and the tail below 10 (`Proto`, `Credentials`, 3 OCI image-label references, 2 `extends` bases that are expressions).

THE TWO OTHER SCOPE NUMBERS, so no column is read alone: whole-corpus (all 3,250 files, 219,981 edges) the same walk reads resolved 42,442 · ambiguous 140,782 (64.0%) · unresolved 35,676, with 1,081 external-verified and 0 unverifiable and 0 refuted. That ambiguity share is why the sample's 1,305 is NOT the lane's ambiguity number, and it is the second reason 815 of the 1,112 land in the ambiguous column rather than resolving.

WHAT WAS TESTED AND REJECTED before any marker was added, on the arbiter's own classifier (census `MARK SIMULATION`, sample scope): marking EVERY unresolved edge refutes 11 claims, 9 of them `imports` whose owner segment is in-project (`kong.deprecation` owner `kong`, `cjson.safe` owner `cjson`, `cmp.types` owner `cmp`), which is the lane's standing refusal to mark module paths now carrying a refutation count; a bare-identifier-only rule marks 2,079 with 0 refuted but is broader than the analyzer's own evidence, and a calls-only rule marks 907 with 0 refuted but cannot separate `insert(x)` from `mine.insert(x)` at the edge — this analyzer publishes the FINAL SEGMENT (LUA-13), which is the documented trap in validation/m14/fixtures/lua/stdlib-external.lua rows D and F. Any widening is therefore its own ruling with its own audit, not a footnote to this one.

decisions.node_type: (the three types the stride reports SILENT: implements, overrides, instantiates)
decisions.question: `bun script/m14/firing-check.mjs LUA` at its default stride reads `7 types fired — implements overrides instantiates SILENT`. Which of the three is a real absence, and which is the instrument's stride? Each needs a whole-population count before it can be called either.
decisions.resolution: RULED PER TYPE, whole-population measured first. (1) `implements` IS ABSENT AND INAPPLICABLE — BD-implements/G1: the pinned grammar produces 100 distinct node types and none of the six that would express a conformance clause, and Lua has no declaration form for a type. (2) `overrides` EMITS: **67 edges** whole-corpus at the current revision (validation/m14/fixtures/lua/measurements/incoming-split-lua-60-all.json, 3,250 files, 219,981 edges, type table `overrides 67`), matching the wave's §3.1 count of 67 in 38 files (luvit 29, kong 23, luarocks 10, snacks.nvim 4, plenary.nvim 1), split 65 `lua_redefinition` at 1.0 + 2 `lua_inherited_member` at 0.95 (BD-overrides-shapes). (3) `instantiates` EMITS: **122 edges** whole-corpus at the same revision, matching §3.1's 122 in 65 files (snacks.nvim 36, luvit 33, plenary.nvim 19, trouble.nvim 13, kong 10, lazy.nvim 4). THE STRIDE IS THE WHOLE EXPLANATION AND IT IS DIRECTLY MEASURED: `NFILES=4000 bun script/m14/firing-check.mjs LUA` — the instrument's corpus for this lane is the kong repo, so 4000 admits ALL 400 of its files with no stride — reads `9 types fired, 400/400 parsed, ... instantiates:8 overrides:3 ... SILENT: implements`. The default 120-file draw is 30% of that population, and the two types' corpus-wide populations are 67 and 122 edges in 38 and 65 of 3,250 files, so a 120-file stride is expected to miss both: it did. NO ANALYZER CHANGE was made for any of the three, and none is due — two already emit at their recorded rates and the third is ruled by the grammar. WHAT WOULD OVERTURN (1): a non-zero count of `implements_clause`/`extends_clause`/`superclass`/`interface_implementation`/`interface_declaration`/`trait_declaration` in validation/m60/lua/grammar-inventory.json.

decisions.status: RULED AT 60 FILES — SUPERSEDED IN SCOPE by BD-ambiguity-full
decisions.question: `npx tsx script/m14/incoming-gate.ts lua lua 60` reads 1,305 ambiguous of 5,415 edges across 566 distinct names. Is any of that reducible without changing what an edge IS?
decisions.resolution:
SUPERSEDED IN SCOPE 2026-10-09 by BD-ambiguity-full, and the numbers below are LEFT VERBATIM because the comparison is the evidence. Every proportion below was measured at `--nf 60` — a 60-FILE key space holding 566 distinct names. At the GATE'S OWN key space (all 3,250 admitted files, 15,326 distinct names) the SAME four-way split reads multiFile 131,914 of 140,782 = 93.7%, NOT 52.4%: a target's declarations can only span the files the key space contains, so a 60-file sample cannot see the cross-file collisions the gate counts. THE BUCKET ORDER SURVIVES; THE PROPORTIONS DO NOT. And the deeper question the ruling answers is answered differently at scale: of 163,583 multiSymbol edges the published name genuinely cannot separate 193 (0.12%), not the majority. ORIGINAL TEXT, unchanged: RULED IRREDUCIBLE AT EDGE IDENTITY, and the split is the evidence rather than the number (`validation/m14/fixtures/lua/measurements/incoming-split-lua-60-sample.json`, census --nf 60, the gate's rule imported, `COMPARE ... AGREE`):

  multiFile                 684 (52.4%)  the colliding declarations are in DIFFERENT files of one project. This analyzer publishes the FINAL SEGMENT of a member read (LUA-13) and Lua resolves `M.foo` at run time through the table, so two modules' `foo` fields are two unrelated declarations that share a name; no field an edge carries names the file or the module.
  oneFileDiffOwner          312 (23.9%)  one file, different owner scopes — locals of two functions. Lua has NO spelling for a caller-scoped local (`f.x` is not a name for a `local x`), so qualifying the target to disambiguate would invent a path the language does not have.
  oneFileSameOwnerSameKind  303 (23.2%)  one owner, one kind, the name declared twice — which IS a Lua construct, and the one this lane already publishes: `overrides`/`lua_redefinition` (last declaration wins in a chunk, confidence 1.0). Both declarations are real, so the collision is the language's, not the analyzer's.
  oneFileSameOwnerDiffKind    6 (0.5%)  the only bucket a symbol-identity change could touch, and it is six edges.

KIND signatures over those 1,305 (variable 1,007 · method|variable 185 · method 51 · function|method 37 · function|variable 18 · function|method|variable 7) and MARKER signatures (contains/no-marker 480 · luaSpecific+relationshipType 444 · luaSpecific 193 calls · luaSpecific+receiver 184 member reads · external-marked 4) agree with that reading: the collisions are bare local/field names, not path spellings.

THE COLUMN IS SAMPLE-DEFLATED, so the sample's number must never be quoted as the lane's: whole-corpus (3,250 files, 219,981 edges, same walk) reads **140,782 ambiguous (64.0%)** with 36,913 ambiguous-by-kind, against 1,305 of 5,415 (24.1%) in the 60-file draw — a stride truncates each project's symbol table, which makes a name whose collision lives in an unsampled file read unique. A reader comparing the two numbers is reading the instrument, not the language.

WHAT WOULD MOVE IT, and why it is not a resolution fix: publishing the qualified path as the TARGET for members (the approach `json` takes, and the gate indexes `qualifiedName` aliases precisely so a lane CAN) would resolve part of the multiFile bucket — at the cost of this lane's member-identity contract (LUA-15, pinned by validation/m14/fixtures/lua/member-identity.expectation.json: identity is container PLUS own name, with the path in metadata). That is a change to what an edge names, not a repair of resolution, and it is recorded here as the option rather than taken silently.

decisions.node_type: (incoming resolution — ambiguous targets, at the GATE's key space)
decisions.status: RULED — cause #1 of the residual is INSTRUMENT SCOPE over a bare-name key space, not edge identity
decisions.question: The gate reads 140,782 ambiguous of 219,981 edges (80.2% residual) over the whole admitted population. BD-ambiguity answered this at 1,305 ambiguous / 60 files and ruled the class irreducible at edge identity. Does that ruling hold at the size the gate actually measures?
decisions.measurement: Three instruments, one population, all on 2026-10-09. (1) BASELINE: `npx tsx script/m14/residual-gate.ts --lane lua` (whole admitted population, production scope) — edges 219,981 · resolved 42,442 · amb(decl) 140,782 · unresolved 35,676 · residual 80.2% · extFAIL 0 · bindFAIL 0 · causeFAIL 0. Artifact validation/m14/fixtures/lua/measurements/residual-gate-lua.txt. (2) THE COLLISION SPLIT AT THE GATE'S KEY SPACE: validation/m14/fixtures/lua/incoming-split.mts --nf 4000 --all (the corpus is 3,250 files, so the sample arm IS the full arm; the log prints both and they are identical). Artifact measurements/incoming-split-lua-full.json + .log. (3) THE LEXICAL DECOMPOSITION: validation/m14/fixtures/lua/ambiguity-split.ts, whose artifact validation/m60/lua/ambiguity-split.json was produced at 3,250 files / 83,906 symbols / 219,981 edges / 0 parse failures / 0 fallback files.
decisions.resolution: CAUSE #1, NAMED AND COUNTED: BARE-NAME TARGETS RESOLVED AGAINST A GLOBAL KEY SPACE. The gate's own marker-set table splits the 140,782 by metadata signature, and the largest single class that maps to ONE type and ONE mechanism is `(no marker)` = 41,592 edges (29.5%), which is EXACTLY the `contains` count: `addContainsRelationships` publishes `owner -> symbol.name` with `{}` metadata, so the target is a bare declaration name and the edge carries nothing else. The collision split at the gate's key space: multiFile 131,914 (93.7%) · oneFileDiffOwner 3,778 (2.7%) · oneFileSameOwnerSameKind 4,551 (3.2%) · oneFileSameOwnerDiffKind 539 (0.4%), across 15,326 distinct names. THE RULING IS LEGITIMATE AND THE EVIDENCE IS THE LANE'S OWN LEXICAL INSTRUMENT, not an argument: over ITS multiSymbol population of 163,583 edges the four-way decomposition reads B1_lineSettled 94,398 (57.7%) · B2b_fileAbsent 63,881 (39.0%) · B2c_noneVisible 5,111 (3.1%) · B3_indistinct 193 (0.12%). `contains` ALONE: multiSymbol 43,854 -> B1 43,739 (99.7%), B2b 0, B2c 0, B3 115. So for the single largest class there is not one edge whose target is absent from its own file, and 99.7% are settled to exactly ONE declaration by Lua's ordinary ORDER rule at the line the edge already carries. The edge is TRUE and its target IS one declaration given (file, line); what cannot use either is the arbiter's bare-name lookup over a global key space. That is INSTRUMENT SCOPE — the same shape as LUA-G6 on the unresolved column — and no analyzer change can express it without replacing LUA-15's container+own-name identity, which BD-ambiguity already declined and this measurement does not reopen. THE TWO DEFINITIONS ARE NOT INTERCHANGEABLE and are never added: the gate's `ambiguousByDecl` is 140,782 (its rule, its key space) and the lexical instrument's `multiSymbol` is 163,583 (bare name PLUS qualifiedName, deduped on file/qualifiedName/kind/line). Each number is quoted with its instrument.
decisions.falsifier: The ruling is legitimate ONLY while the name-inexpressible class stays small. MEASURED: B3_indistinct is 193 edges, 0.12% of the 163,583 multiSymbol population, and 115 of those are `contains`. If a later run shows B3_indistinct growing materially — or shows `contains` with a non-zero B2b_fileAbsent, i.e. a contains edge whose target is absent from its own file — this ruling is REFUTED and the identity change becomes the work. The counterpart falsifier for the collision split: if `--nf 3250 --all` did NOT move multiFile away from 52.4%, the 60-file proportion would have been the population's and BD-ambiguity would stand as written. It moved to 93.7%, so it does not.
decisions.note_not_run: The FIRST attempt at the collision split was KILLED BY THE LOCK, not by the measurement: `flock -w 600 9` timed out (exit 9) because another lane held .bb-heavy.lock, so the run never started. It is reported as NOT RUN, never as a negative result. The re-run waited `-w 3600` and completed (SPLIT_EXIT=0).

decisions.status: FIXED — the module-path class is a CHECKABLE FILE CLAIM, not an exclusion and not an external marker
decisions.question: `imports` reads 5,645 unresolved of 6,601 edges (85.5%) at the whole admitted population, and 5,485 of those are DOTTED module paths. R6 of docs/analyzers/real-lua-analyzer.md proposed a `metadata.moduleTarget` EXCLUSION — 'a module path is not a declaration, so do not count it'. Is an exclusion the right mechanism, and is anything about this class checkable from a single file?
decisions.measurement: TWO WHOLE-POPULATION GATE RUNS, ONE CHANGE BETWEEN THEM, plus four supporting instruments. (1) BEFORE: `nice -n 10 npx tsx script/m14/incoming-gate.ts lua lua 0`, HEAD bad316c7d, analyzer sha256[:16] bc9de4bc3fd0bd0b, 3,250 files, 0 parse failures, 0 degraded — `imports 6601 / resolved 76 / amb 880 / unresolved 5645 / extOK 0`; TOTAL `219957 / 84034 / 99190 / 35652 / extOK 1081`, extFAIL 0, bindFAIL 0, causeFAIL 0. (2) AFTER: the same command at HEAD beb03387f with ONLY src/ast/real-lua-analyzer.ts changed (sha256[:16] d35f6e6f6d1f3339) — `imports imports       6601     76        0         880        120        1796        3849    0       0        0        0       0         0        0`; TOTAL `TOTAL         219957   84034     41592     99190      28643      31803       4930    0       0        0        0       0         0        0`; `of those 4930 verified: 1081 by owner lookup in the key space, 3849 against the project's own pubspec files + file list`. (3) PRICE BEFORE EMITTING: validation/m14/fixtures/lua/tools/imports-claim-pricing.mts --files=25 --compare-guard — a labelled stride sample of 358 of the 3,250 admitted files: 740 sampled-unresolved, 544 VERIFY, 0 would-refute, 196 residue, candidate multiplicity `1=544` (every claimed edge had exactly ONE admitted candidate, so no base ordering decided an outcome), and `GUARD-vs-PROBE 740 compared, 0 disagreements`. (4) THE REFUTATION COLUMN OVER THE WHOLE POPULATION: the guard binds on `statSync` and the arbiter refutes on `git ls-files`, so the two can disagree only on a `.lua` file present on disk and untracked — MEASURED 0 of 3,250 present (tracked 3,252, of which the same 2 the gate reports as absent). (5) THE CONTROL: tools/require-file-claim-control.ts, 10 arms, ALL PASS — four positive arms whose claim the ARBITER verifies via verifyFileClaim, four arms that must write NO claim (absent module, no projectRoot, escaping target, a directory that is not a module file), one that the target is unchanged, one for the `pcall(require, …)` site. (6) ADDITIVITY: tools/claim-preservation-dump.ts over 181 strided files / 14,585 edges — MOVED 0, CLAIMED added 276 / removed 0 / changed 0. Fixtures both arms: `summary: {"lua":{"pass":13,"fail":0}}`.
decisions.resolution: FIXED BY THE SHARED FILE CLAIM, and the mechanism is the argument. A `require` target is a MODULE NAME and the gate's key space holds DECLARATIONS, so the edge can never resolve — but 'names no symbol' is not 'says nothing checkable'. `require("a.b.c")` now carries `metadata.importProjectFile` (`FILE_CLAIM_KEY`) when the shared guard `src/ast/file-claim.ts` confirms an admitted `.lua` file on disk, and the arbiter checks that path against the project's own admitted list. WHY NOT THE EXCLUSION R6 PROPOSED: an exclusion says DO NOT LOOK, and it is unfalsifiable; a file claim is REFUTED when the project does not carry the file, which is why the programme prices it before emitting it. WHY NOT `isExternal`: this lane priced that arm on 2026-10-09 and it REFUTED 1,560 of 5,485 edges (`imports lapis.application` has owner `lapis` and the project declares `lapis`), i.e. the claim was false as stated. THE ARITHMETIC IS THIS LANE'S AND THE GUARD IS NOT: dots become directory separators, `X.lua` is tried before `X/init.lua` (the order the default `package.path` writes), and four bases are tried in a named order — the project root (`./?.lua`), the requiring file's own directory (busted), the prefix ending at the file's first `lua/` segment (Neovim runtimepath / OpenResty plugin layout, which supplied 420 of the 544 sampled hits), and `<fileDir>/lua/`. The admitted-extension clause, the inside-the-project clause, the 1 MB cap and the `statSync` stay inside the guard. THE CLAIM CANNOT RAISE `resolved` AND CANNOT EXCUSE A GAP: `classifyEdge` reads a `projectFile` claim only inside `if (decls === 0)`, so on an edge the key space already answers it is never even consulted — unlike the binding and `remoteRef` claims, which are refuted by a resolving target. WHAT IT DOES NOT CLOSE: the residue is real and counted — 3,849 of the 5,645 moved to an `extOK` claim verified against the project's own file list and **1,796 remain unresolved**, on the same marker signature `luaSpecific+relationshipType` — the LuaRocks toolchain and the rocks this corpus does not vendor (`luarocks.util`, `luarocks.fs`, `luarocks.core.cfg`, `tap`, `argparse`, `compat53.module`, `pl.file`); the claim does not touch them, `extFAIL` stays 0, and `unresolved` is the TRUE reading for them..
decisions.falsifier: The claim is legitimate while BOTH hold, and each has a run-able falsifier. (1) NO REFUTATION: a claim the project does not confirm must read `extFAIL`, which must stay 0 — refuted by any AFTER run showing `imports extFAIL > 0`, or by a `.lua` file present on disk and untracked in any corpus repo (measured 0 of 3,250 on 2026-10-11; a single such file under a claimed module path re-opens the hole). (2) DETERMINACY: the claim names ONE file, and on the priced sample every claimed edge had exactly one admitted candidate — refuted by a priced run whose multiplicity histogram shows edges with TWO OR MORE admitted candidates, which would make the emitted path a choice among true options; the base order would then need its own evidence. (3) THE POPULATION CLAUSE: a caller that hands the analyzer a relative `projectRoot` (or a root the file is not under) gets `path.relative` escapes, the guard refuses them, and NO claim is written — a SILENT smaller number, the direction `file-claim.ts` documents for `magicConstants`. The BEFORE/AFTER pair is the check that this clause does not suppress in the measured path: the gate passes an absolute repo root, and 3,849 edges moved.

gap._description: Confirmed unemitted semantics, numbered LUA-G*. A gap is a tracked work item, never a gate failure: the gate fails when a gap exists that no `design_decision` rules, and when a ruling names a construct the pinned grammar no longer produces. Every entry carries the measurement that established it, from an artifact committed under validation/m60/lua/ or validation/m14/fixtures/lua/measurements/, and the instrument is named because a count without its instrument is not checkable. THE FIELD WAS ABSENT UNTIL 2026-10-09 — not empty, unstated — which is why the fleet's machine-readable gap total did not include this lane; absence of the field is exactly the state the board cannot distinguish from 'no gaps'.

gaps.node_type: implements_clause, extends_clause, superclass, interface_implementation, interface_declaration, trait_declaration
gaps.missing: `implements` is never emitted, and the reason is a fact about the language rather than a search failure: Lua has no `class` or `interface` declaration form, conformance is duck typing and is not written down. A conformance clause would have to be a node type, and the pinned grammar produces none of the six that would express one.
gaps.evidence: validation/m60/lua/grammar-inventory.json — 100 distinct node types produced across the corpus (namedTypesProduced in this file), NONE of the six. validation/m60/lua/conformance-probe.json — instrument B (tree walk, node+field anchored) found the nearest expressible shapes: 4 `b1_namedSuperclassCall` occurrences in 1 file and 288 `b2_conformanceAssert` occurrences in 99 files, i.e. conformance is EXERCISED at run time and never DECLARED. Ruled by BD-implements; falsification condition recorded there (a non-zero count of any of the six node types).
gaps.ruling: RULED-SOUND, not a defect. Nothing to implement unless a Lua dialect with a declaration form appears.

gaps.node_type: function_call (supertype argument to a locally-defined factory)
gaps.missing: A supertype written as an ARGUMENT to a locally-defined factory — `class(prototype, properties, parent)` in luarocks/vendor/argparse.lua, where the factory's own third parameter IS the parent — produces no `extends` edge. The analyzer reads `setmetatable`/`__index` shapes only.
gaps.evidence: validation/m60/lua/supertype-arg-probe.json — ROLE-RESOLVED (the slot is read from the callee's own `parameters` node, never a positional guess): 13 factories declare a supertype-role parameter, **7 written supertype arguments across 5 files** pass a NAME there (`class` x2 in argparse.lua:277/:328 passing `Parser`/`Argument`, `add` x3, `_each` x1, `is_required_field` x1), and 13 further role slots are present but pass an expression or nothing. The same probe shows why the pre-role probe read 0: it read argument index 2 for every `class(...)`, and argparse's convention puts the parent THIRD.
gaps.ruling: OPEN, small and named. Closing it needs a per-provider convention (which parameter of THIS factory is the parent), which the probe already derives by role; the count is the size of the work, not an estimate.

gaps.missing: Two inheritance shapes are unemitted: a constructor that binds its own metatable (`setmetatable(self, { __index = Base })`) — 45 sites across 42 files — and a base written as an EXPRESSION (`setmetatable(opts or {}, defaults)`) — 374 sites across 218 files. Neither names a declarable base at the edge.
gaps.evidence: validation/m60/lua/ontology-census.json probe B8, recorded in BD-overrides-shapes: 501 supertype links split into 79 `crossTable` (both sides declared tables), 45 `derivedIsSelf`, 3 `selfLink`, 374 `unresolvedBase`. Only the 79 carry a named base on both sides.
gaps.ruling: OPEN and deliberately not guessed. The derived table is reachable only by evaluating the constructor, and nothing in the parse tree says which table it returns; closing the 374 would require interprocedural evaluation. Recorded as a limit with its size, per BD-overrides-shapes.

gaps.missing: An `imports` target naming a MODULE cannot be resolved to a symbol and is deliberately not marked external, so it stays in the arbiter's `unresolved` column. One file cannot tell a sibling module from a luarocks rock: of the module targets measured, some name a file that IS in the corpus and some name a file that is not.
gaps.evidence: validation/m60/lua/external-marking.json — 6,601 `moduleTarget` edges across the corpus (the class left unmarked), against 16,195 that the rejected name-list rule would have marked. validation/m60/lua/classb-origin.json — 5,485 `imports` edges: **2,425 whose module file exists in the corpus, 3,060 whose module file is absent**, 699 with a segment present in a module file. And the refutation count, measured 2026-10-09 with the arbiter's own classifier (validation/m14/fixtures/lua/measurements/incoming-split-lua-60-sample.json, `markSim`): marking the unresolved module paths REFUTES 9 claims — `kong.deprecation` (arbiter owner `kong`), `cjson.safe` (owner `cjson`), `cmp.types` (owner `cmp`) and 6 more — because the owner segment IS declared in the project.
gaps.ruling: OPEN, and the shape of the fix is known: a project-wide module→file map (the 2,425/3,060 split is the population it would decide), not a per-file rule. Until then the class is reported rather than swept, and it is now a counted refusal rather than a stylistic one.

gaps.missing: A `calls` edge records the callee's FINAL SEGMENT and no receiver (LUA-13), so `mine.insert(x)` and a bare `insert(x)` arrive as the same edge `calls -> insert`. `references` edges DO carry a `receiver`; `calls` edges do not. The consequence is that a member call and a runtime global are indistinguishable at the edge, which is why no external marker can be attached to the class without a rule that is wrong for one of them (see the rejected rules measured in validation/m14/fixtures/lua/measurements/incoming-split-lua-60-sample.json, and lua's own stdlib-external.lua rows D and F).
gaps.evidence: validation/m60/lua/external-marking.json `rejectedRule` (the name-list rule measured at 16,195 edges — it cannot tell `table.insert` from a user's own global `insert`). validation/m60/lua/incoming-audit.json — `calls` targets `not-declared-anywhere`: 5,631 edges, top names `list_extend` 130, `nvim_buf_get_name` 108, `tbl_contains` 100, i.e. host globals of the Neovim/Wireshark/Kong surfaces. Measured 2026-10-09 with the arbiter's classifier: a calls-only external rule marks 907 sample edges with 0 refuted, and a bare-identifier rule marks 2,079 with 0 refuted, but NEITHER can exclude the member calls, because the fact that separates them is not on the edge.
gaps.ruling: OPEN with a cheap fix available: publish the callee's shape (`identifier` vs index expression) in `calls` metadata, which the analyzer already computes in `callee()` (:2177) and throws away. That single fact turns 5,631 unmarked host-global edges into a class a rule can name, and it is the reason the widening was NOT taken in this pass rather than a claim that it cannot be.

gaps.missing: Half of the arbiter's unresolved column at `lua lua 60` is not an analyzer fact at all: 1,112 of 2,222 edges name a declaration the SAME project publishes in a file the 60-file stride did not include (297 with one declaration, 815 colliding), and 417 more name one in another project.
gaps.evidence: validation/m14/fixtures/lua/measurements/incoming-split-lua-60-all.json — all 3,250 admitted files parsed, the gate's rule imported, `COMPARE ... AGREE` against the captured gate run: declaredInProjectFull 1,112 (inProjectUnique 297 / inProjectColliding 815), declaredInCorpusOtherProject 417, nowhere 693. Whole-corpus scope for contrast: 219,981 edges = 42,442 resolved / 140,782 ambiguous (64.0%) / 35,676 unresolved.
gaps.ruling: NOT A DEFECT — an instrument-scope effect, recorded so the column is never read as 2,222 broken edges. A complete-key-space run moves every one of the 1,112 out of `unresolved`; 815 of them land in `ambiguous`, which is the number the next pass should work on.

excluded.label: implements
excluded.from: BD-implements: 'RULED, and `implements` is the type it rules. Instrument A: the pinned grammar produced 100 distinct node types across 1,875 corpus files, and NONE of the six node types that would express it is among them'

coverage._from: BD-ontology: 'NINE are emitted — calls, uses, contains, imports, references, exports, extends, overrides, instantiates — and ONE is ruled: `implements`.'

_implemented_measured._unit: edges published through the production path. TWO populations, and they disagree because they ARE different populations — this is the lane where that distinction was measured rather than assumed. (1) WHOLE-CORPUS CENSUS: 3,250 files / 219,981 edges across 19 repos, artifact validation/m14/fixtures/lua/measurements/incoming-split-lua-60-all.json (`perTypeFull`), which carries EVERY edge and its resolution outcome. (2) WHOLE-POPULATION FIRING over the lane's own corpus dir (kong, 400 files, no stride): validation/m14/fixtures/lua/measurements/firing-check-whole-population.txt. The two are NOT the same measurement and neither is the other's error: `overrides` is 67 corpus-wide and 3 in kong alone, `instantiates` is 122 corpus-wide and 8 in kong. The corpus-wide figure is recorded here because this map answers 'does this type fire in the population', and a single repo is a sample of it.

coverage._implemented_measured_note: SELF-REFUTATION RECORDED: the first version of this map took `edges` as the SUM of the corpus-wide resolution outcomes, which counts each edge once but reads 117 for `overrides` and 123 for `instantiates` against the lane's own recorded 67 and 122 — the spec's LUA rulings and docs/analyzers/real-lua-analyzer.md §4 both say 67 (in 38 files) and 122 (in 65 files). THIS BLOCK RECORDS THE LANE'S FIGURES and states the range rather than picking the largest: a per-type map whose number does not match the ruling it substantiates is worse than no number.
